To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the material properties gradient, crack configuration, and loading combination affect the magneto-electro-mechanical field intensity factors and energy release rates of functionally graded magnetelectro-elastic strip.

the field intensity factors, the energy release rates and the crack opening displacements for the magneto-electro-permeable crack problems are larger than those of the magneto-electric impermeable crack problems.

the magneto-electro-mechanical field intensity factors and energy release rates of a functionally-graded magneto-electroelastic strip with an embedded or edge crack depend on the loading combination parameter and material gradient parameter, and the crack is magneto-electric impermeable or magneto-electric permeable, respectively, which is the main contribution of our research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of a magneto-electro-mechanical crack problem in a strip.
the fracture mechanics of a functionally magneto-electroelastic material.
the analysis of an anti-plane problem of a functionally gradient magneto-electro-mechanical strip containing an embedded crack and an edge crack.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the field intensity factors of the functionally-graded magneto-electro-elastis strip increase with the increase of material gradient parameter, and the field intensity factors for the edge crack are greater than those of the embedded crack.
the magneto-electric coupling effect is more pronounced for the edge crack case.

, for an embedded crack or an edge crack perpendicular to an edge of a functionally gradient magneto-electroelastic strip, the energy release rate and the field intensity factors are all dependent on the loading combination parameter and the material gradient parameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magneto-electric coupling has a significant effect on the field intensity factor and energy release rate for the embedded crack and edge cracks.
the field intensity factors are dependent on the material gradient parameter and the loading combination parameter.
the energy release rates are always larger than the corresponding values in the homogeneous case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field intensity factors are sensitive to the loading combination parameter and the material gradient parameter.

, for a functionally graded material, the energy release rate and the field intensity factor are affected by the material properties and their variation, which is different from the case of homogeneous materials.
the field intensity factors, energy release rates and the stress intensity factors of a magneto-electro-elastically impermeable crack are larger than those of a magneto- electrically permeable crack.
